nh_kennel_wall.blurb: Kennel Wall is a small, quiet cliff at Rumney, a short uphill scramble past New Wave Wall. It holds 19 routes, mostly bolted (14 sport, 5 trad), and the bulk sit between 5.10 and 5.12, with a handful of easier lines and one 5.13. The cliff splits into two sections: the left half mixes cracks and faces with some awkward steep moves, while the right half has steep, crimpy face climbs, several of them originally led on gear and later bolted. The two halves face different ways, so you can sometimes dodge sun or wind by switching sides. It makes a handy short-route option when the busier Rumney walls are crowded.

nh_12_mt_adams_king_ravine.blurb: King Ravine is the big glacial bowl on the northern flank of Mt Adams in the Presidential Range. Best known as a winter snow and ice objective, it also has scattered summer boulder problems among the huge blocks on the ravine floor, plus some easy rock scrambling. The 19 climbs here are almost all boulder problems, running mostly from VB to V3 with a few much harder lines up to V11, and a single top-rope. Expect a long hike in on the Air Line and Short Line trails from the Appalachia lot off Route 2, so this is a day for carrying pads, not a quick roadside stop.

nh_colossal_cluster.blurb: Colossal Cluster is a group of house-sized boulders ringed by smaller blocks, part of the Swamp Boulders in the Boulder Natural zone of Pawtuckaway State Park. All 19 problems are bouldering, with most between V0 and V6, a few steps harder, and one very hard line at the top end. Plenty of pads and spotters help on the bigger blocks. Reach it by heading upstream from the large Yosemite Boulder, or via the shortcut on the initial approach, then crossing a damp stretch of swamp to the rocks, where the landings are mostly dry and flat.

nh_inferno_atlantis_area.blurb: This section of Whitehorse Ledge's steep South Buttress above North Conway holds 19 trad routes, mostly technical face climbing on slabby, edgy rock. Grades cluster around 5.10, with a few at 5.9 and below and some harder lines at 5.11 and 5.12. Many lines are multi-pitch and combine into longer outings, with a mix of bolts and gear. The cliff is a very warm south-facing wall that turns hot in summer, but it is a good pick for late fall and sometimes winter days when other walls are too cold. Descent is by rappel or the hiking trail from the top slabs.
nh_inferno_atlantis_area.parking_note: Use the upper parking lot beside the hotel and pick up the yellow-blazed hiking trail from there.
nh_inferno_atlantis_area.approach: Follow the yellow-blazed trail left past the first golf tees as it curves around the South Buttress. At a small cairn, take the climbers' path to the right and climb steeply to the base of the big slab, then traverse right along its foot and scramble up its left side to reach the routes.

nh_up_in_smoke_area.blurb: Up in Smoke Area is a boulder cluster in the middle of the Devil's Den bouldering zone at Pawtuckaway State Park, tucked off the trail up the hill from Boulder Natural. All 19 problems are bouldering and the range is wide: a few easy lines, then a solid middle of V4 to V9 testers, with a couple of very hard problems at the top. Several of the park's best-known hard lines live here, so it suits strong boulderers more than beginners. Boulders are scattered among talus below the cliffband, and the easier, less-visited lines can be mossy.

nh_the_deep.blurb: The Deep is a medium-sized boulder field in Pawtuckaway State Park, spread across the valley on both sides of a brook. Boulders run medium to large, with tops mostly 10 to 15 feet and decent landings. Its 19 problems span from easy scrambles up to a few V6 and harder lines, with most in the V0 to V4 range, making it friendlier than some of the park's hard-focused zones. It lies over the hill from New Natural, so the two can be combined in one day. The walk in is about a mile from the South Mountain lot along connecting trails.

nh_deers_leap_windham.blurb: Deers Leap is a small local crag in Windham, in southern New Hampshire's Merrimack Valley, with 19 trad routes and some top-rope options. Climbing is mostly easy to moderate, with a spread from 5.5 to 5.9 and a few harder lines at 5.10 and 5.11. Three main walls make up the area: the Main Face above a pond, Andy's Cliff in the middle, and Porcupine Cliff. It is a good after-work spot for new climbers and families, and rarely busy. The rock is weathered with some rounded cracks and loose spots, lichen on some lines, and ticks and bugs are heavy, so bring repellent.

nh_the_very_nice_crag.blurb: The Very Nice Crag is a small, quieter corner of Rumney, built around a steep gully on the left side of the Prudential formation, and was once known as NW Passage. It has 18 routes, mostly sport (13) plus a few trad lines and a top-rope. Grades start around 5.7 and centre on 5.10 to 5.12, with five 5.12s and a single 5.13, so it suits intermediate to strong climbers. Climbs include bolted faces, cracks and roofs, and a short cave offers cover from passing showers. It is a mix of styles away from the crowds, but not a place for small children or dogs.
